question: With spare cash, should a household with a 4% mortgage pay it down rather than buy shares?
answer: Every euro repaid earns exactly the mortgage rate, guaranteed, with no fees and no bad years. Shares may average more, but only on average: a household that invested in 2007 watched its savings halve while the mortgage stayed whole. A smaller loan also shrinks the monthly bill that would hurt most after losing a job.
move: Whichever side you took, how soon the money might be needed decides it.
ask: If my income stopped next year, which use of my spare money would I be glad I had chosen?
counterpoint: Over long periods shares have paid well above 4%: since 1900, world equities have beaten inflation by roughly 5% a year. Money sunk into bricks cannot easily be taken out in a crisis, while an invested pot can. Twenty years of compounding at the higher rate usually leaves a far larger cushion than a cleared mortgage.
source: Dimson, Marsh and Staunton, Triumph of the Optimists
reference: Dimson, Marsh & Staunton, Triumph of the Optimists: 101 Years of Global Investment Returns, Princeton University Press, 2002
